findings.observation: Provider-specific diagrams encode live authentication, pagination, retry, and storage claims that contradict current provider configuration and normative medallion rules.
findings.method: Manual claim-to-config/SSOT comparison plus rg across provider API integration diagrams and configs/providers/*.yaml.

evidence.observation: The ChEMBL flow asks whether an API key is available and offers cursor, offset, and scroll pagination; its retry decision sends 'No' to Error and 'Yes' to backoff.
ChEMBL is configured as auth_type: public and pagination.strategy: offset (line 15).
The ChEMBL diagram states that Bronze is written to Delta Lake.
The normative rule defines Bronze as append-only JSONL + zstd and reserves Delta Lake for Silver and Gold.
PubChem, PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and UniProt diagrams say cursor pagination, while each corresponding config declares offset; CrossRef and OpenAlex are the two accurate cursor cases.

findings.expected: Every provider diagram must describe the provider's current auth, pagination, retry, and medallion storage contract, with claims traceable to config/code/SSOT.
findings.actual: ChEMBL contains contradictory auth, pagination, retry, and Bronze storage branches; four additional providers label offset pagination as cursor pagination.
findings.impact: Operators and maintainers can implement or diagnose the wrong authentication, paging, retry, or persistence behavior from a published engineering artifact.
findings.root_cause: Provider diagrams were cloned from a generic flow and are not guarded against provider-config or normative storage drift.
findings.remediation: Correct the ChEMBL API and medallion sources, replace cursor labels in the four offset-provider sources, regenerate only their SVG siblings with pinned tooling, and add a config-to-diagram contract test.
findings.automation: Add a provider diagram contract test that asserts auth_type, pagination.strategy, and Bronze storage terminology against current configs and RULES.md.

findings.observation: Nine tracked SVG artifacts fail the repository's fallback-text normalization check, while the broad manifest exposes only one of those failures.
findings.method: python -m scripts.diagrams fix-svg-text --check; fix-foreign-object --check; fix-svg-styles --check; check-svg-text on default, extended, broad, and full corpus.

evidence.observation: Nine SVGs need 192 fallback text nodes in total: architecture 24, 26, 43-48 and views 39-medallion-invariants-full.
The broad manifest fails only on architecture/24; the remaining eight failing artifacts are outside this gate.
Twenty-three tracked SVGs still need the canonical CSS injection.
Twenty-five sequence SVGs would be modified by the canonical link-style postprocessor.

findings.expected: Tracked SVGs must be reproducible postprocessed artifacts with readable fallback text and canonical styling, and required gates must cover newly added artifacts.
findings.actual: Nine SVGs retain foreignObject-only text, 23 lack canonical CSS injection, 25 need link harmonization, and the broad gate catches only one of the nine text failures.
findings.impact: Text can disappear in non-HTML SVG consumers and artifact consistency is not enforced for recently added diagrams.
findings.root_cause: The corpus has outgrown the curated manifests and post-render fixers are not enforced over every tracked SVG.
findings.remediation: Run the supported pointwise fallback/style/link postprocessors on the named artifacts, review the text-as-code sources, and extend a required manifest or add a full-corpus normalization gate without committing PNG output.
findings.automation: Run check-svg-text and canonical style assertions against every tracked SVG in CI, or enforce source-to-SVG coverage for all new diagrams.

findings.observation: The supported Docker fallback creates and passes an args-only host Puppeteer config that prevents Chromium discovery inside the pinned Mermaid container.
findings.method: Run the official checks entry with MMDC_FORCE_DOCKER=1 on a representative class diagram; compare direct pinned docker render with and without the generated -p config.

evidence.observation: ensure_puppeteer_config writes only sandbox args when no host Chromium is found; host detection cannot discover the container's /usr/bin/chromium-browser.
The official path exits 1 because Puppeteer cannot find Chromium in the pinned 10.6.1 container.
Direct pinned renders pass for flowchart, sequence, state, and class samples when the host args-only config is not passed.

findings.expected: MMDC_FORCE_DOCKER=1 must provide a fully reproducible pinned renderer usable by the official checks command.
findings.actual: The image works directly, but the official wrapper path overrides browser discovery with an incomplete host-generated Puppeteer config.
findings.impact: Contributors without the exact host mmdc cannot run the documented full pinned render gate; a full 441-source syntax render was therefore blocked in this audit.
findings.root_cause: Host-specific Puppeteer configuration is reused inside a container with a different executable path.
findings.remediation: When Docker mode is active, omit -p or generate a container-specific config with its Chromium executable; cover both host and Docker modes in tests.
findings.automation: Add a wrapper smoke test that renders one diagram with MMDC_FORCE_DOCKER=1 and the pinned local image.

findings.observation: The ELK fixer misclassifies valid multiline Mermaid init directives as missing ELK configuration.
findings.method: python -m scripts.diagrams apply-elk --dry-run plus direct evaluation of has_elk_init against an existing multiline init block.

evidence.observation: The predicate requires init, layout, and elk to occur on the same physical line.
A source whose multiline init already contains layout: elk is reported as needing elk_init; 17 files are false-positive modifications.

findings.expected: The fixer must recognize semantically equivalent one-line and multiline init directives and be idempotent in dry-run/check mode.
findings.actual: Multiline directives are not recognized, so 17 already-ELK diagrams are proposed for modification.
findings.impact: Running the advertised fixer can inject duplicate initialization directives and create unnecessary source/render churn.
findings.root_cause: ELK detection is line-oriented rather than directive/block-oriented.
findings.remediation: Parse or concatenate the complete Mermaid init directive before checking layout and elk; add one-line, multiline, and unrelated-init regression fixtures.
findings.automation: Unit-test fixer idempotence over both supported init syntaxes.

findings.observation: The link-style differentiation fixer silently scans an obsolete, nonexistent diagrams/mermaid directory.
findings.method: Static path inspection, path existence check, and python -m scripts.diagrams differentiate-linkstyle --dry-run.

evidence.observation: MERMAID_DIR is hard-coded to docs/02-architecture/diagrams/mermaid and main globs only *.mermaid there.
The command exits 0 after scanning 0 files although the active corpus contains 441 source diagrams.

findings.expected: The public fixer must scan the active canonical source tree recursively or fail loudly when its configured root does not exist.
findings.actual: It targets a removed path and reports a successful zero-file run.
findings.impact: Operators receive a false-success signal and link-style drift remains untouched.
findings.root_cause: A legacy directory layout remained embedded in the fixer after the canonical tree moved.
findings.remediation: Resolve the current diagrams root, recurse over supported source suffixes, reject an empty corpus, and add a CLI regression test.
findings.automation: Add a test asserting that the default corpus exists and the CLI discovers representative .mmd and .mermaid files.

findings.observation: Generated ChEMBL dataflow drift is triggered solely by a repository-wide source date, not by a semantic change in the generator's actual inputs.
findings.method: python -m scripts.diagrams generate-dataflows --check; generate to audit preview; normalize old/new generated dates and compare every reported file.

evidence.observation: _source_date runs git log over all configs and src/bioetl rather than the dataflow's exact inputs.
The check reports 14 stale text artifacts: six diagrams, six descriptions, the IR JSON, and the pipeline passport.

evidence.command: Compare generated preview to tracked files after replacing 2026-08-12/2026-08-18 metadata dates
evidence.observation: All 14 normalized files are byte-equivalent; normalized_non_date_mismatches=0.

findings.expected: The generated-artifact gate should change only when the generator or an input contributing to the ChEMBL dataflow changes.
findings.actual: Any unrelated non-merge commit under configs or src/bioetl advances the embedded date and invalidates all 14 artifacts.
findings.impact: CI and contributors see noisy stale-artifact failures and must create broad documentation churn unrelated to the diagram's claims.
findings.root_cause: Freshness metadata uses a repository-wide last-change date as generated content.
findings.remediation: Derive provenance from the exact config/code inputs or exclude display-only generated dates from drift equality while keeping a stable input hash.
findings.automation: Add a regression test proving an unrelated src/bioetl change does not alter generated dataflow artifacts.

findings.observation: The published view inventory records 162 tracked Mermaid views while the current corpus and diagrams index contain 165.
findings.method: Count tracked docs/02-architecture/diagrams/views/*.mermaid and compare the governance inventory with diagrams-index.md.

evidence.observation: The baseline claims 162 files and its table omits three singleton overview views.
There are 165 files; the omitted singletons are 21-idempotent-processing-guards-overview, 23-reproducible-run-contract-overview, and 24-data-runtime-quality-map-overview.

findings.expected: The published measured inventory must match the tracked corpus and enumerate every view family.
findings.actual: The baseline is lower by three and omits three architecture-derived singleton views.
findings.impact: Governance readers and future audit automation operate from an understated corpus size.
findings.root_cause: The inventory was not refreshed when three singleton views were added.
findings.remediation: Update the baseline to 165, add the three singleton rows, refresh the verified date, and add a count/table consistency test.
findings.automation: Validate the inventory table against tracked view filenames in the existing diagram corpus regression suite.
